title: How to Live: 27 Conflicting Answers and One Weird Conclusion
author: Derek Sivers
vetoReason: The central purpose is personal life guidance through 27 competing sets of actionable directives. This is established from the author's description and contents, not the title alone. The reflective format does not remove the life-support purpose.
note: No hard exclusion: aphoristic prose and an artistic framing do not make this a poetry collection or fiction. V7 applies to its central life-guidance purpose. Deliberate contradiction is a rhetorical design, not by itself an epistemic veto. Counterfactual assessment retains weak empirical support. Philosophy is central (T12=-10); T11=0.
notes: Claims are primarily personal judgments and directives, not an evidence-based investigation.
Compares life priorities but offers little integration of technological or institutional systems.
Perspective switching may help decisions; advice lacks explicit boundary conditions.
Few developed causal explanations connect directives to outcomes.

D=7/10, moderate confidence from author contents and contrasting reader reports. Short opposing chapters add distinctions between priorities; some maxims restate familiar advice. Brevity is not treated as proof of density.
Many tensions between commitment and freedom are durable, though aphorisms need context.
Little direct relevance to the main technical and industrial domains.
Experienced entrepreneur and writer; no corresponding specialist validation of the general life claims.
The opposing-chapter structure is clear and memorable.
Concise prose, with precision limited by intentionally absolute directives.

title: KetoFast
author: Joseph Mercola
vetoReason: The publisher and author describe a diet and fasting protocol intended to improve health and treat disease. Nutrition and health advice are the central purpose, directly meeting V7.
note: General-reader health advice is not a specialist technical curriculum under H3. V7 applies before any need to establish additional epistemic vetoes. Counterfactual score is low-confidence and does not validate the protocol. Disease and health dominate (T11=-10); T12=0. The publisher establishes original 2019 publication, overriding the conflicting Goodreads 2017 field.
notes: The inspected author account makes broad health and detoxification claims without establishing controlled evidence for this combined protocol; empirical support remains weak in this assessment.
Combines several dietary practices but does not integrate the preferred industrial or institutional layers.
A personal dietary protocol offers little transferable strategic utility.
Contains metabolic explanations, but moving from mechanism to clinical benefit is insufficiently established.

D=4/10, moderate confidence from Karpathy's reading report and contrasting readers: basic points recur with limited added explanation. The reported repetition is distinct from the evidential weakness.
Protocol-specific advice is less durable than established general biological mechanisms.
Minimal direct fit for the preferred domains.
Medical credential and commercial endorsements do not establish research consensus for the proposed protocol.
Practical organization is identifiable, but readers report uneven presentation.
Promotional and categorical language limits precision.

title: The Productivity Project: Accomplishing More by Managing Your Time, Attention, and Energy
author: Chris Bailey
vetoReason: The author's stated purpose and practical tactics concern personal productivity and life management. Self-experimentation supports a self-help program, not a sustained study of industrial productivity or organizing technical work.
note: General personal productivity advice is not technical training under H3 and does not fall under H7's specific communication or HR categories. V7 applies based on its life-management purpose. Counterfactual scoring retains limitations of uncontrolled self-experiments. Neither thematic deduction applies: the subject is personal productivity rather than one of the specified central themes.
notes: Personal experiments and selected research can suggest hypotheses but do not establish general causal effectiveness.
Relates time, attention and energy; wider institutional and technical systems are peripheral.
Some prioritization and distraction-control heuristics are reusable, subject to work constraints.
Explains selected behavioral mechanisms but relies heavily on personal experience.
D=5/10, moderate confidence from author overview and contrasting reader reports. Several practical distinctions are useful, but repeated framing and familiar advice receive substantial criticism.
Many everyday attention problems persist; individual tactics depend on circumstances.
Efficiency is relevant, but the main focus is personal habits rather than technical systems.
Experienced practitioner and communicator, without demonstrated specialist research standing in the inspected evidence.
Accessible practical structure; memoir and advice can repeat.
Generally direct prose, with broad claims that exceed the self-experiment's scope.
